newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kyushu Oil says shipped jet fuel to Alaska.
newsitem.headline: Kyushu Oil says shipped jet fuel to Alaska.

text.p: Kyushu Oil Co Ltd said on Monday that it shipped about 34,000 kilolitres of jet fuel to Alaska in mid-July under a third-party processing agreement placed by Itochu Corp, a leading Japanese trade house.
A Kyushu Oil spokesman said it was the first time the company had exported jet fuel. He declined to give the pricing or other details of the deal.
He said the contract was clinched in early June, prior to an announcement by Japan's Trade Ministry on deregulating oil product exports starting in July.
The deregulation measures included scrapping the need to file for permission for each overseas oil product shipment.
Oil exporters now need to file for approval only once a year.
Kyushu Oil started exporting refined products through third-party processing about seven or eight years ago.
The spokesman said the company is mostly geared to refining for sale in the domestic market and exports products only when there is extra capacity.
